            'category' => optional($p->category)->label,
        ]);
    }

    public function productsByCategory(Category $category)
    {
        return Product::where('category_id', $category->id)->get();
    }

        return $product->reviews->map(fn ($r) => [
            'rating' => $r->rating,

    public function productsWithoutCategory()
    {
        return Product::whereNull('category_id')->get();
    }

    {
        return $category->products->map(fn ($p) => [
            'label' => $p->label,
            'reviews_count' => $p->reviews->count(),

    {

    {
        return Review::latest()->take(20)->get()->map(fn ($r) => [
            'product' => $r->product->label,
            'user' => $r->user->name,
        ]);
    }

input.reason: Without eager loading, each order triggers one query for its user and one for its items (N+1). Loading 'user' and 'items' up front reduces this to 3 queries total.
Accessing $item->product inside the loop issues one query per item. Eager loading 'items.product' (plus 'user') collapses this to 3 queries total.
$item->product inside the loop triggers one query per item. Eager loading 'items.product' reduces it to 2 queries.
$p->category is lazy-loaded per product (N+1). Eager loading 'category' fetches all categories in one query.
$r->user inside the loop triggers one query per review. Eager loading 'user' on the reviews query reduces it to 2 queries.
$p->reviews->count() in the loop triggers one query per product. Eager loading 'reviews' makes it a single additional query (counts computed in memory).
$o->items->count() in the loop triggers one query per order. Eager loading 'items' reduces this to 2 queries total.
Each review lazy-loads its product and user (2 queries per review). Eager loading both relations drops it to 3 queries total.
